questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving at the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving at the same speed.
questions.explanation: When being passed, keep your speed steady. Do not speed up or slow down. Let the other vehicle pass safely and merge back into your lane.

questions.question: Any amount of alcohol in your blood may affect your:
questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol can affect your judgment and coordination. This makes it harder to drive safely. Driving after drinking any amount of alcohol is dangerous and illegal.

questions.question: In a car with airbags, where should children age 12 and under sit?

options.text: The bed of a pick-up truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back seat.
questions.explanation: Airbags can hurt children. All children age 12 and under must sit in the back seat of a car that has airbags.

questions.question: Which of these is dangerous in a work zone?

options.text: Not watching for workers and equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, slow down and keep more distance between your car and others. Watch carefully for workers and machines.

questions.question: If the road ahead is flooded, what should you do?

options.text: Do not drive through the water. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through the water. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through flooded roads. The water may hide dangers you cannot see. Find a different route instead.

questions.question: How can you prevent yourself from becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the speed limit.
Follow the car in front of you closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and focus on your driving. Do not take other drivers' actions personally. Leave plenty of time for your trip, follow speed limits, and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road will be slippery ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is starting.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a divided highway is ahead. Stay on the right side of the median.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices in construction and maintenance work areas?
questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers mark work zones. Drive carefully when you see orange warning signs on the road.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on water instead of the road. How can you prevent it in rain?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: In rain, drive slower to prevent hydroplaning. If you drive too fast, your tires may slide on the water and lose grip on the road.

questions.question: What should you do before passing on a two-lane road?

options.text: Check how far away oncoming vehicles are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check how far away oncoming vehicles are.
questions.explanation: Oncoming vehicles may be going faster than they appear. Always make sure there is enough space to pass safely. If you are not sure, wait until the other vehicle passes before you try to pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Look for vehicles in the direction you plan to go, then proceed.
Let all vehicles go first, no matter when they arrive.
Look for traffic in all directions before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for traffic in all directions before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, you must stop completely and look in all directions for traffic before proceeding.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: You should use cruise control near railroad crossings to keep a steady speed.
You must stop at railroad crossings when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at railroad crossings and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at railroad crossings when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Drive carefully near railroad tracks.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, you should:

options.text: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Always wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt. Using only one part greatly reduces your protection. If you have an automatic shoulder belt, also buckle your lap belt.

questions.question: A distraction when driving is:

options.text: Anything that causes you to take quick action while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can happen anytime and anywhere. They can cause crashes, damage, injuries, and death.

questions.question: Before returning to your original lane after passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing is allowed, look for both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. Only then can you safely return to your original lane.

questions.question: Adjust your rearview and side mirrors:

options.text: Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Your safety and others' safety depends on what you do before driving. Before moving, adjust your seat, adjust your mirrors, fasten your safety belt, and secure items in your vehicle. Do not adjust mirrors while driving.

questions.question: You should yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
At all times, even if the pedestrian is breaking traffic laws.
Only if the traffic light allows pedestrians to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if the pedestrian is breaking traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your vehicle. Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC) and reduce alcohol's effects on a body.
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: The only way to sober up is to wait for your body to remove the alcohol from your system. Nothing else, including eating and drinking, will speed this up.

questions.question: Before starting the engine, you should:

options.text: Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Before starting your car, buckle your own safety belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs too.

questions.question: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on a thin layer of water instead of the road. To prevent hydroplaning in wet weather, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down when driving on wet pavement to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: When it is dawn, dusk, raining, or snowing, it is hard to see and be seen. What should you turn on to let other drivers know you are there?
questions.correctAnswerText: Your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights anytime you cannot see other vehicles clearly or when other drivers cannot see you. Turn on your low beam headlights whenever you use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights, what must you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, pull to the right edge of the road and stop. Park parallel to the curb. On one-way streets, drive toward the nearest road edge.

questions.question: When can you drive off the road to pass another vehicle?

options.text: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
If there are two or more lanes going in your direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never drive off the paved road or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Why are barriers, drums, cones, and signs used in work zones?

options.text: To make drivers frustrated about slow traffic.
To keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for both workers and drivers. Watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers wearing bright vests. They warn you and show you where to go.

questions.question: What should you do before backing your vehicle?

options.text: Walk around the entire vehicle to check for people or obstacles behind it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk around the entire vehicle to check for people or obstacles behind it.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, walk completely around your vehicle to check for people or obstacles. Look over your shoulder and out the rear window when backing. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and let trains go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains go first.
questions.explanation: A round sign means a railroad crossing is ahead. This sign is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. It tells you to slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When daylight starts to fade, what lights should you use to help others see you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: As daylight fades, turn on your low beam headlights so others can see you. Only use high beam headlights when you are alone on an open road with no other drivers.

questions.question: What is the best way to change lanes?

options.text: When a car is in your blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and carefully. Only change lanes when you need to. Every lane change increases the risk of an accident.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Side road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you there is a side road intersection ahead.

questions.question: Which statement about driving is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake hard to make sure you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Press the brakes gently with increasing pressure so your vehicle stops smoothly.
